entries.finding: short-side coverage of the AUD-07 long cases (C11 / C13a / C13c / C13d / C13g / TP gap)
entries.title: Short-side mirrors of every long case: NEWCORE acceptance expectations for the SHORT side
entries.rationale: Every long case is mirrored to the short side: each symbol's market reflected around its own flat base price (a candle [o,h,l,c] becomes [2P-o, 2P-l, 2P-h, 2P-c], so the declared path relative to the position and the ATR are unchanged), signals and side flipped. Expectations are the CORRECT causal NEWCORE outcome computed from first principles (scratch calc.py, Decimal arithmetic), not from an adapter: fees are on the notional and slippage is multiplicative, so mirrored prices do not give mirrored R and every number was recomputed. The legacy rules that are not fixed (C11, C13a, C13c, C13d, C13g, the backtest TP gap) reproduce on the short side exactly as the mirror of the long; each is recorded as a strict-xfail known divergence bound to this record, with the observed mismatch list from a blind run checked by hand against the mirrored legacy rule. G-GAP-DCA-S-01 moves the candle-285 low to 100.8743 so the leg ends just past the recomputed short basket target 100.874358 (the long's 99.125 vs 99.124884), with a per-trade engine path-step tolerance of 0.0002 USDT.
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors on cff3f88; blind probe of both legacy adapters on every new case (scratch probe.py)

entries.finding: exit-code vocabulary: STOP_CROSSED (bot market close) distinct from STOP_HIT (exchange stop fill)
entries.title: STOP_CROSSED cases (long + short): a trailing level recomputed at a candle close is already through the price
adapters_changed: legacy_engine: stop_crossed -> STOP_CROSSED (was folded into STOP_HIT); flatten / resync / stop_failed / basket_tp_part mapped (bc948d9)
entries.rationale: Pins the STOP_HIT vs STOP_CROSSED distinction with a fully causal trigger and no path artefact: zero-range candles make the Wilder ATR of each closed candle shrink by 1/14, so the 2-ATR trailing level rises at every candle-close decision until, with ATR(285), it lies above the price 100 (short: below). A stop order cannot rest on the wrong side of the market, so the correct NEWCORE outcome is a bot market close at the next decision - the open of candle 286, which is that candle's first path point - booked as STOP_CROSSED at 100 x (1 -/+ slippage), R -0.07; the resting exchange stop at 99.96 (100.04) is never touched. The legacy engine journals exactly this (stop_crossed, required). The legacy backtester closes at the same bar and price but writes why='stop', i.e. STOP_HIT: recorded as a strict-xfail known divergence (code only) bound to this record. Expectations from first principles (scratch calc.py prints the ATR / level schedule).
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors on bc948d9; blind probe of both legacy adapters (scratch probe.py)

entries.finding: B2 coverage: partial exit (smallest expressible slice: C25 zero part)
entries.title: Partial take-profit that floors to zero at the exchange step: nothing sent, nothing marked, full target taken
entries.rationale: A real partial fill is not expressible in the v1 one-row-per-position trace (P2-3b, needs the AUD-08 event trace); the smallest partial-exit slice that IS expressible is the AUD-02 C25 rule: a tp1 part that floors to zero at the instrument step (step 5, qty 5, part 2.5) sends no order and marks nothing done, so the whole position reaches the 2 R target as one row, TP_FULL R 1.9385932. Legacy adapters are not_applicable (they refuse slot.tp1 and instruments by design); the expectation was cross-checked outside the pack by running both legacy models directly with these exchange rules (scratch xcheck_tp1.py: replay take_profit 19.3859, backtester tp 19.385932 with one recorded zero partial).
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors on cda8f58; scratch xcheck_tp1.py

entries.finding: B2 coverage: outage (smallest slice: exchange-side stop fills while the bot is cut off)
entries.title: Stop filled on the exchange during a bot outage: STOP_HIT in the candle of the fill, booked from the exchange record
entries.rationale: Smallest outage slice whose correct outcome needs no new policy: the protective stop rests on the exchange, so it fills during the outage exactly as in the fault-free twin G-STOP-L-01; the bot must book it from the exchange order record with the exchange time (i_out 282, STOP_HIT, R -1.059307099) rather than at the recovery candle, as a resync, or with a second close. Outage window in integer UTC ms, seed null (deterministic). Legacy adapters not_applicable: the replay cannot inject an outage (check_unsupported raises NotExpressible).
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors on 47932c0; twin G-STOP-L-01

entries.finding: B2 coverage: restart (smallest slice: restart between entry and time exit)
entries.title: Bot restart mid-trade does not reset the C11 holding clock: time exit still at the close of i_in + N - 1
entries.rationale: Smallest restart slice: a 5-minute process restart 1 minute after the open of candle 281 (integer UTC ms, seed null), with no candle close inside the downtime. With durable state (AUD-05) the lot is restored with its fill time, and the AUD-07 C11 rule counts candles from the fill candle, so the correct outcome equals the fault-free twin G-TIME-L-01: TIME_EXIT at the close of 283, R -0.004666666667. A restart that resets or re-derives the clock from the process start fails it. Legacy adapters not_applicable (no restart injection in the replay).
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors on 717c8d7; twin G-TIME-L-01

entries.finding: B2 coverage: ambiguity (smallest slice: lost answer to a filled entry)
entries.title: Entry filled on the exchange with its answer lost: resolved from the order record, booked as the one filled trade
entries.rationale: Smallest ambiguity slice: the first entry order is executed by the exchange (truth filled) but its answer is lost (seed null, deterministic). Under the AUD-03 contract the order is resolved only from the exchange's final record and never re-sent while unresolved, so the correct outcome equals the fault-free twin G-STOP-L-01: one LONG lot of 5 from candle 280, STOP_HIT in 282, R -1.059307099, final lots 0. A second entry (double size), a phantom lot or an untracked position fails it. The not_filled truth is left out on purpose: whether NEWCORE retries an entry at a later decision is an open policy, not a causal fact. Legacy adapters not_applicable.
entries.evidence: branch golden-short-mirrors; twin G-STOP-L-01

entries.finding: the NEWCORE management core caps adds at one by design
entries.title: G-GAP-DCA-L-01 / G-GAP-DCA-S-01: NEWCORE adapters record the one-add cap (NC07-ONE-ADD-CAP); the historical two-add contract is unchanged
entries.rationale: Codex ruling (NC-07 golden follow-up): keep the historical two-add golden cases, do not retire or rewrite them, and record a stable NEWCORE-incompatible divergence for the intentionally one-add core. The NC-07 management core enforces a single bounded add in the core (its planned risk reserves exactly one add), so on these three-level DCA baskets it takes only the first safety order. Both NEWCORE adapters move from pending_adapter to known_divergence with the new registry ID NC07-ONE-ADD-CAP; the expectation, the market, the slot, the legacy adapters and the legacy_backtest AUD07-C13A divergence (still bound to its own record) are unchanged. The observed lists are the NC-07 core prediction until the NC-08 adapter runs. The NEWCORE contract for the same gap-through-the-add path is the separate one-add case G-GAP-DCA-ONEADD-L-01 / -S-01.
entries.evidence: scratchpad oneadd/compute.py: newcore.management.run on an export of nc-management 5e17446 (Decimal; q0 = 0.408163265306, q1 = floor(1.5 x q0) at 1e-12): LONG exit candle 286, pnl 0.898994187, R 0.089899; SHORT exit candle 286, pnl 0.896924800, R 0.089692

entries.finding: NEWCORE one-add DCA contract (gap through the single add, basket target re-anchored to the new average)
entries.title: G-GAP-DCA-ONEADD-L-01 / -S-01: the NEWCORE one-add DCA contract next to the historical two-add cases
entries.rationale: Codex ruling (NC-07 golden follow-up): add a separate one-add NEWCORE case for the new contract while the historical two-add cases stay unchanged (CORR-0066 records NC07-ONE-ADD-CAP on them). Same market shape as G-GAP-DCA-L-01 / -S-01 with slot.dca n 1, scale 1: the single add is gapped at the open and fills at the open with the entry slippage, then the basket target avg +/- 1 ATR re-anchored to the new average is reached in candle 285 (its extreme moved to just past the recomputed target). Expectations are the NC-07 core result (Decimal) checked by hand. The legacy engine reproduces them exactly (required); the legacy backtester shows the existing AUD07-C13A defect (gapped add without slippage), recorded as a strict-xfail divergence bound to this record with the observed list from a blind run. NEWCORE adapters stay pending_adapter until NC-08. Extended tier: every coverage class is already in core via G-GAP-DCA-L-01.
